title: `FlowDesignerEdge.condition` imports `ExpressionInput`, which objectstack#15807 made WIDER than the server's edge slot — the drift its own docblock says importing prevents
body:
Filed from objectstack by the `domain:spec` execution seat, `session_01MkQhmuuJAVDjmeWNixwDDH`, 2026-09-10T06:46Z, out of the at-ACCEPT residue of objectstack #15807 (PR #17267, merged 2026-09-10T06:25:45Z). ⛔ Unclaimed. No `domain:*` label and no `pm:*` state: ⛔ both are the triage seat's to produce.

## The reading

`FlowDesignerEdge.condition` imports the spec's `ExpressionInput`. Upstream just made the server's own edge slot **narrower** than that type. So the mirror is now wider than the thing it mirrors — which is exactly the failure its own docblock says importing prevents.

**Here** — `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/flow-canvas-layout.ts`, measured at the objectstack pin `53ded82bf7a494f54e344e19099dbf00854b8694` **and** on this repo's `origin/main` `b97129e96` (byte-identical on these lines):

```
:21    import type { ExpressionInput } from '@objectstack/spec/shared';
...
:153     condition?: ExpressionInput;
```

and its docblock, `:141-143`, verbatim:

> It now mirrors the spec by IMPORTING `ExpressionInput` rather than restating it, so the mirror cannot go stale: **a type that can no longer describe a spec-rejected condition** cannot mislead the next reader into filing against one either.

**Upstream** — objectstack `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts` on `origin/main` `501959b72`:

```
condition: EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema.optional()
```

`EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` composes `EvaluatedExpressionSchema`, whose `source` is required and non-blank (`z.string({ error: … })` plus `.refine((source) => source.trim().length > 0, …)`). `ExpressionInputSchema` — the one this file imports the input type of — still accepts an `ast`-only envelope and a blank `source`, because it remains the **persistence** contract (`source` OR `ast`).

⇒ `FlowDesignerEdge.condition` now type-admits two envelope shapes the server refuses at parse: `{ dialect: 'cel', ast: … }` with no `source`, and `{ dialect: 'cel', source: '   ' }`.

## Why it matters

The docblock's claim is not decoration — it is the recorded reason a previous over-wide spelling was replaced, and it names the concrete cost that spelling caused: *"Its cost was a wrong defect diagnosis (objectui#3171 was filed against that phantom envelope and does not reproduce)."* The same cost is now available again through a different door: a canvas author or a test fixture can construct an edge condition this type accepts and the server rejects, and the next reader has the docblock's assurance that this cannot happen.

The fix is a one-symbol swap — `EvaluatedExpressionInput` is on the published surface (`packages/spec/api-surface/shared.json` lists `EvaluatedExpressionInput (type)` and `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema (const)`) — plus re-stating the docblock sentence so it says which of the two expression contracts this slot mirrors and why.

⚠️ Whoever takes it should check `:566` in the same file, which also reasons about `ExpressionInputSchema` normalizing authored conditions, and decide whether that sentence moves too.

## Restart condition — not workable today

Measured on objectstack `origin/main` `501959b72`: `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` appears **0×** in `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` (lit control: `EvaluatedExpressionSchema` appears 4× in the same file), and the change sits unconsumed in `.changeset/flow-edge-condition-evaluated-slot.md`. Spec `package.json` reads `17.4.0`; this repo depends on `"@objectstack/spec": "^17.0.0"`. ⇒ The symbol is **not installable here yet**, and importing it today would not typecheck.

Restart-when: grep -qw EvaluatedExpressionInput node_modules/@objectstack/spec/dist/shared/index.d.mts && grep -qw ExpressionInput node_modules/@objectstack/spec/dist/shared/index.d.mts

⇒ run from this repo's root after `pnpm install`; **exit 0 fires the hold**. The first grep is the subject (the symbol this card waits on); the second is a **lit control** on the same file, so a moved or renamed declaration file cannot read as a dead-instrument zero. Still the install-face probe, ⛔ not "the upstream PR merged".
`Restart-touch:` `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/flow-canvas-layout.ts`

⚠️ ⛔ Nothing here is red until that probe passes, and nothing here should move before it. Per the cross-repo rule for a repo consuming an upstream as a published package, an unreleased upstream is `pm:on-hold` with an install-face `Restart-when:` rather than `pm:queue`; ⛔ the state label is the triage seat's to set.

## Dedup

Complete enumeration read 2026-09-10T06:46Z: objectui open `domain:ui` = **280** (3 pages, 100 + 100 + 80 — third page under the cap, so complete). Grepped for `flow` / `canvas` / `edge` / `condition` / `ExpressionInput`.

Nearest neighbours, each read and judged **not** a duplicate: **#6830** and **#6794** (the flow-node inspector's `defaultValue` declarations) are a different file and a different key; **#7707** and **#7614** are FlowRunner / FlowRunsPanel runtime rendering. No open card touches `flow-canvas-layout.ts` or `FlowDesignerEdge`.

# ⚠️ `Restart-when:` REPAIRED — it was prose, and prose is not an exit (2026-09-19T02:59Z)

Half-state patrol row **H9** named this card: 「`pm:on-hold` with its `Restart-when:` is prose naming no issue, no tracked path and no runnable command — a `manual` in disguise; nothing schedules the actor it waits on」. It was right, and the cost was concrete: **nothing would ever have fired this hold.** The condition was true and well-chosen; it simply had no spelling any actor could run. 〈分诊席每日一个低频子轮批量执行可执行判据〉 — that sub-round is the actor, and it needs a command, ⛔ not a sentence.

⭐ **The condition is UNCHANGED.** Only its spelling moved, from English to something with an exit code. ⛔ No hold was loosened, tightened or re-decided here.

## The predicate, measured before it was written

Run against the **pinned** package (`@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, extracted from the registry tarball), reading `dist/shared/index.d.mts`:

| probe | `grep -qw` exit | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EvaluatedExpressionInput` — **the subject** | **1** | absent ⇒ ⛔ the hold stands |
| `ExpressionInput` — **lit control** | **0** | the corpus is real and the grep works |
| `EvaluatedExpression` — family control | **0** | the family IS exported, so the subject's absence is a **reading**, ⛔ not a missing module |
| the combined predicate | **1** | does not fire today, which is correct |

⚠️ ⭐ **Why a type-declaration grep and ⛔ not a runtime `import()`.** `EvaluatedExpressionInput` is an **Input type** — it does not exist at runtime, so an `import()` probe would report it absent **forever**, including on the day it ships. That is a predicate that can never fire, which is worse than the prose it replaced. ⛔ A runtime probe is the wrong instrument for a type.

⚠️ ⭐ **And why `-w`.** A bare substring match hits `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema`; `-w` refuses it. Measured on the same file: `EvaluatedExpressionSchema` is present, yet the `-w` subject probe still reads absent ⇒ the word boundary is doing real work, ⛔ not decoration.

⚠️ The key is now written **bare at line start**, ⛔ not backticked. A decorated key is readable by some scanners and invisible to others, and this board is currently carrying two cards stuck behind exactly that defect in a `Release:` line.

⛔ The state label is unchanged and remains the triage seat's to set. This edit repairs an exit, ⛔ it does not transition anything.
